Subject: Billing model question — how do token floors work for streaming sessions?

Hi Priyom,

Quick question as we're finalizing the SOW: your team quoted a 10k token minimum per active user per month for our pilot. We run a mix of short high-frequency prompts (2–20 tokens) and occasional long summaries (~6k tokens). How does Redwood apply the minimum — is it per call, per session, or aggregated across the month? Also: when a response is streamed, do you bill on generated tokens only or include in-flight partial frames?

Need to reconcile with our internal chargeback model. Can you send a short example calculation for a mixed-week workload?

Thanks,
Jessica
Procurement Lead, AcmeHealth

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing model question — how do token floors work for streaming sessions?

Jessica — thanks for the great questions. TL;DR: the floor is evaluated at the customer-account/month level (not per-call or per-user) and streaming is billed on generated tokens (we do not double-bill for transport frames). Below are short bullets + a concrete example attached.

- Minimums: monthly customer-level floor (10k tokens) amortized across all calls for the month; we do not apply a per-request floor unless you opt into the seat-based pilot.
- Aggregation: input + output tokens are summed across the billing window; partial tokens from incremental frames are rounded up at the service-side tokenization boundary (see Excel examples).
- Streaming: billed on final tokens emitted (and the input tokens consumed). We do account for tokenization differences between pretokenized inputs and raw text; edge diffs are small.
- Proration: if you start mid-month we prorate the floor by calendar days. Example: month has 30 days; 15-day trial -> floor reduced to 5k tokens.

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Proposal_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf (proposed commit and discount), token-calculation-examples.xlsx (worked examples for short bursts + long summaries).

I'll paste a quick worked example below:

Example week (approx):
- 10k short prompts at 10 input + 5 output tokens = 150k tokens
- 200 long-summary calls at 6k output + 3k input = 1.8M tokens
- Total = ~1.95M tokens for the week. Monthly would be ~7.8M tokens. Floor is 10k/month — so no floor impact here. Floor mainly matters for very low-volume pilots or per-user seat pilots.

If you'd like, Vanessa can run an amortized quote showing how the floor affects unit price at lower volumes and provide alternate packaging (commit tiers or per-seat pilot).

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Adding a couple clarifications from pricing ops:

- Rounding: we round up to the nearest whole token after service-side tokenization. We do NOT round per-frame during streaming; rounding happens once per request at finalization to avoid small-frame inflation.
- Minimum application: when accounts are under the floor in a billing month we credit them the delta in the next invoice if agreed in the SOW (we sometimes apply a one-time pilot credit instead of carrying an ongoing credit).
- Discounts: for committed volume we can offer a blended unit price with a reduced or waived floor for the pilot (example in attached PDF: 3-month pilot with commit of 250k tokens/month -> floor waived and 15% discount).

Ben — can you add a short set of math scenarios (low / mid / high) with our proposed blended rates? Jessica — I put the numbers in the attached proposal; happy to tweak if you have a target effective price.

-V

Forwarding a quick calc I prepared.

-- calc snippet pasted inline --
Scenario A (pilot small):
- Estimated consumption: 25k tokens total/month
- Standard unit rate (listed): $0.0008 per token
- Floor: 10k tokens -> customer charged for 25k tokens (above floor) so no additional floor uplift. Effective price = 25k * $0.0008 = $20.00

Scenario B (micro pilot):
- Estimated consumption: 6k tokens/month
- Floor triggers (10k) -> billing would show 10k * $0.0008 = $8.00; if SOW includes pilot credit we would invoice actual 6k and apply a one-time credit of $2.40 in next invoice (or waive floor).

Scenario C (long-summary heavy):
- Estimated consumption: 8M tokens/month -> commit pricing applies, example blended unit = $0.00045/token with 12-month commit.

Notes: prorate logic for starts/stops is calendar-day based. Partial-token rounding edgecases are included in the attached spreadsheet.

Ben Carter

Jessica / Procurement team — thanks for the redlines. Confirming Redwood's position on the three asks:

1) Proration language: happy to accept exact language you proposed. Will include clause: "Monthly floor will be prorated by calendar days in first and last partial billing months."

2) Pilot credit: for pilots below 10k/month we will apply a one-time credit equal to the difference between the floor and actual usage for the first billing cycle (documented in SOW). If you extend to a second pilot month we can discuss waiving the floor for month two as part of a short pilot concession.

3) Rounding appendix: accepted. We will add: "Token counts will be determined by Redwood service-side tokenization and rounded up to the nearest token once per request finalization. Streaming frames are not separately rounded."

Next steps: we've updated the SOW (attached) and put it into DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/AcmeHealth-SOW-v3 — Jessica, once countersigned we will trigger provisioning.
